scenario: LLEX.11.1's binary prefix is `0b`, lowercase only. So `0B` and `0Bps` are unit literals (LLEX.11.3.1): zero of `units.computer`'s byte alias `B` and byte-per-second alias `Bps`. Each is compared against a slot of its own dimension, so the rule compiles only if both resolve to those units. Beside them `0b101` is still the binary integer literal, compared to an `Int` slot, with `bit` and its alias `b` in scope to show that the lowercase prefix wins over a unit named `b`. A compiler that takes an uppercase prefix reads `0B` as a binary prefix with no digits and `0Bps` as one whose digits stop at `p`, and refuses the rule. The library is the shipped `stdlib/units/computer.ds`, on every fixture's search path ([RCTS.1.2.14]).
rules_ds:
from units.computer import bit, byte, byte_per_second

schema Link scope logical:
    id: String key
    queued: byte mutable
    throughput: byte_per_second mutable
    flags: Int mutable

rule r:
    Link l where l.queued > 0B and l.throughput > 0Bps and l.flags == 0b101
->
    log info "x"
